cards.heading: SNMP
cards.body: An SNMP manager (NMS) polls agents on network devices (Get, GetNext, GetBulk) and can change values (Set) on UDP 161. Agents send unsolicited Traps, or acknowledged Informs, to the manager on UDP 162. The objects are defined in MIBs, each identified by an OID.

cards.heading: SNMP versions
cards.body: SNMPv1 and v2c authenticate with a community string sent in clear text: RO for read-only, RW for read-write. SNMPv3 adds users with authentication and encryption (noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv, authPriv).
cards.example:
snmp-server community NETMON ro 10   ! read-only, managers allowed by ACL 10
snmp-server location HQ-Rack-3
cards.mnemonic:
The c in v2c stands for community: v1 and v2c send a community string in clear text. v3 replaces it with real users.
v3's levels go up in pairs, where Auth is "who you are" and Priv is privacy (encryption): noAuthNoPriv, then authNoPriv, then authPriv.
RO reads, RW writes.

cards.heading: Syslog
cards.body: Devices send event messages to a syslog server on UDP 514. Every message has a facility, a severity (0-7) and a mnemonic. The trap level sends that level and everything more severe.
cards.example:
%LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Gi0/1, changed state to down
  facility LINK, severity 3 (errors)

logging host 10.0.0.50
logging trap warnings      ! sends 0-4

cards.heading: Severity levels
cards.example:
0 emergencies   1 alerts   2 critical   3 errors
4 warnings      5 notifications
6 informational 7 debugging
cards.mnemonic:
"Every Awesome Cisco Engineer Will Need Ice cream Daily": Emergencies 0, Alerts 1, Critical 2, Errors 3, Warnings 4, Notifications 5, Informational 6, Debugging 7.
The lower the number, the worse the news. 'logging trap 4' sends level 4 and everything more severe (0-3), but not the chattier levels 5-7.

cards.heading: Where logs go
cards.body: Console (on by default), the VTY session (terminal monitor), the RAM buffer (logging buffered, read with show logging) and external servers (logging host). Add timestamps so logs can be correlated. The buffer survives logging out but not a reload.
cards.example:
service timestamps log datetime msec
logging buffered 16384 informational

cards.heading: TFTP and FTP
cards.body: Both copy files such as IOS images and configs. TFTP (UDP 69) is simple: no login, no directory listing, and it does its own acknowledgements. FTP (TCP 21 control, TCP 20 data in active mode) has usernames and passwords but sends them in clear text. FTP's control connection (TCP 21) carries commands such as the login and file requests; separate data connections carry the files. FTP is the better choice for a big IOS image: TCP is reliable over lossy links and it supports logins. In copy commands the source comes first, then the destination.
cards.example:
copy running-config tftp:
copy ftp: flash:
ip ftp username admin
ip ftp password s3cret
